archive_scope: witness-led; no fixed canon or book-count limit
purpose: Build readable continuous texts where possible while preserving the identity, age, language, coverage, and textual differences of every manuscript witness.

witness_traditions.name: Dead Sea Scrolls
witness_traditions.role: Primary organizing reference for Hebrew and Aramaic scriptural writings wherever a relevant Qumran witness survives.
witness_traditions.dating_note: Individual manuscripts are generally dated from the last centuries BCE through the first century CE; dates must be recorded per manuscript, not assigned collectively as one date.
witness_traditions.handling_rule: Preserve each Qumran manuscript and fragment separately with its Qumran identifier, exact coverage, transcription basis, and lacunae. Do not fill a DSS lacuna and label the supplied wording DSS text.

witness_traditions.name: Septuagint and Greek witnesses
witness_traditions.role: Early Greek translation and manuscript evidence; use as a comparison and supplement where the same writing and passage are represented.
witness_traditions.dating_note: Translation activity began in the third century BCE; surviving Greek manuscripts have individual dates and must be catalogued separately.
witness_traditions.handling_rule: Distinguish translation wording, manuscript reading, and later edited Septuagint editions. Do not treat Swete or another edited edition as a direct transcription of one ancient codex.

witness_traditions.name: Samaritan Pentateuch
witness_traditions.role: Independent textual tradition for the Five Books of Moses and a comparison witness.
witness_traditions.dating_note: The textual tradition is ancient; surviving complete Samaritan codices are generally medieval. Qumran manuscripts can preserve pre-Samaritan or related textual forms.
witness_traditions.handling_rule: Keep Samaritan readings distinct from Qumran pre-Samaritan texts and from medieval Samaritan codices. Do not claim the date of a tradition as the date of a surviving copy.

witness_traditions.name: Masoretic manuscripts
witness_traditions.role: Hebrew comparison witnesses, including the Cairo Codex of Prophets, Aleppo Codex, and Leningrad Codex.
witness_traditions.dating_note: Major surviving Masoretic codices are medieval; proto-Masoretic textual forms are also represented among the DSS.
witness_traditions.handling_rule: Identify the exact codex and manuscript date. The Leningrad Codex is one witness and must not define the archive's scope or canon.

witness_traditions.name: Ethiopic / Ge'ez tradition
witness_traditions.role: Versional witness tradition for writings preserved in Ge'ez, including writings whose Hebrew or Greek witnesses are fragmentary or absent.
witness_traditions.dating_note: Translation traditions can be ancient while surviving codices are later; record translation date estimates separately from the date of each physical manuscript.
witness_traditions.handling_rule: Identify the Ge'ez edition or manuscript, its source language where known, and its editorial basis. Do not present a translation as the original-language witness.

witness_traditions.name: Other ancient versions
witness_traditions.role: Syriac, Latin, Coptic, Armenian, and other versional witnesses where relevant.
witness_traditions.dating_note: Date each translation tradition and each surviving manuscript independently.
witness_traditions.handling_rule: Use only where the work and passage are demonstrably represented; preserve versional wording separately and identify translation-mediated readings.

display_modes.label: Actual English reading
display_modes.description: Display only the continuous English text of the writing. Do not insert study descriptions, manuscript metadata, translation notes, or research commentary into the reading. Keep source attribution outside the reading body.

display_modes.label: Manuscript witness only
display_modes.description: Show only text directly preserved by the selected witness; leave damaged or missing areas visibly blank.

display_modes.label: Reconstructed reading
display_modes.description: Show a continuous reading where supported, with every supplied segment linked to its actual source witness in the reading's separate source record.

display_modes.label: Compare witnesses
display_modes.description: Show each witness independently so differences, omissions, additions, and translation effects remain visible.

display_modes.label: Study and manuscript evidence
display_modes.description: Display descriptions, dating, authorship, historical setting, preservation, manuscript metadata, variants, and research references separately from the actual reading.

reconstruction_workflow: Identify one writing once in the master writing catalogue; do not create duplicate writing records for each manuscript tradition.
Register every physical manuscript, fragment, codex, or versional witness as a separate witness record.
Map exact passage coverage and source coordinates before using a witness to supplement a gap.
Display the oldest directly preserved text first, while allowing an earlier or more reliable parallel witness to take precedence where evidence warrants.
When a witness does not preserve a segment, supplement only from a named witness preserving the same passage; record the source and textual relationship.
If no reliable witness supplies the segment, retain an explicit unrecoverable gap.
Keep reconstructed reading, diplomatic witness text, and editorial translation as separate data layers.
notes: The age of a textual tradition, the estimated date of composition, and the date of a surviving physical manuscript are separate facts.
The DSS do not preserve every writing or every passage; absence from the DSS is not evidence that a passage never existed.
A continuous reconstructed display is an editorial aid, not a claim that one ancient manuscript contained the complete displayed text.
No reconstruction is populated by guessing; passage-level evidence and source coordinates are prerequisites.
